response.answer: Anion gap and albumin-corrected anion gap are emerging as valuable biomarkers for predicting sepsis outcomes in emergency department patients. Machine learning models enhance their predictive accuracy for sepsis-related mortality. Recent studies highlight their significance in intensive care settings.

results.content: Further analysis showed that the risk of death of SA-AKI patients within 28 days during hospitalization in the ICU was increased when AG ≥14 mmol/L. • Anion gap (AG) levels can predict the death risk of patients with sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) during hospitalization. • The risk of death of SA-AKI patients within 28 days during hospitalization in the ICU was increased when AG ≥14 mmol/L.
